To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of COMTA on ACTH release depend on the presence or absence of the low-expression variant of MAOA, and that 5-HTT interacts with MD susceptibility in cortisol regulation.
the regulation of the HPA-axis is modulated by genetic variation in serotonin transporter, catechol-O- methyl transferase and monoamine oxidases A and B, in interaction with gender.
genetic variation in 5-HTT (and possibly in MAOA), COMT and gender interact in the regulation of the endocrine response to acute stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic and environmental factors that contribute to the development of MD.
the identification of genetic variants that contribute to the regulation of the HPA-axis.
the genetic modulation of the neuroendocrinological stress response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic variation in the 5-HTT promoter, COMT, and MAOA genes are associated with the endocrine response to stress, and the genetic susceptibility to stress is modulated by the interaction between these genes.
the genetic regulation of HPA-axis activity depends on the presence of multiple polymorphisms and their interaction with gender.
the genetic variation in the monoaminergic genes, especially 5-HTT gene, is associated with the HPA-axis activity in the stress conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulation of the endocrine system in response to stress is a complex process, which depends on the interaction between multiple monoaminergic gene variants and gender, and that these genes are also involved in the stable-state regulation of the endocrinological stress response.

genetic variation in monoaminergic systems is involved in the regulation of stress-related endocrine responses and that the genetic effects are modulated by the interaction of the genes and gender, as well as by the interaction of genes and MD susceptibility.

polymorphic variations of the genes coding for 5-HTT (rs25531), MAOA (MAOA- uVNTR) and COMT (COMT-Val158Met) as well as the interaction between MAOA- uVNRT and COMT-Val158-Met, and gender modulate the HPA-axis response to acute psychological stress in healthy subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic regulation of the stress response is complex and that the effects of genetic variation are context-dependent.
genetic polymorphisms in the monoaminergic system interact to modulate HPA-axis response to acute stress, and that this modulation depends on gender.
the genetic architecture of stress-related disorders is complex, and it is not possible to identify a single gene as a risk factor.
